aspects.says: The listener form calls back once, with the answer or with null on expiry, and throws ISOException when it refuses; the caller's future must complete in every case.
basis: section:4.5 The Asynchronous Form Calls Back Once, With an Answer or With null

aspects.says: request() does not check the link: on a down link the message waits in the queue for the timeout and may go out later, so the client asks isConnected() first and reports the host as unavailable.
basis: section:4.4 A Request on a Down Link Waits in the Queue

aspects.says: A response's listener runs on the adaptor's receiver thread, so a slow listener delays every answer on the link.
basis: section:4.5 The Asynchronous Form Calls Back Once, With an Answer or With null

aspects.says: Code looks a MUX up by name when it uses it and depends only on the MUX interface, so it survives late deployment and redeploys, and a pool can take the name.
basis: section:4.7 Code Names a MUX and Never Keeps One
section:4.7.1 A Pool Takes the Name's Place

aspects.says: request() returns null when no answer comes in time; that is an unknown outcome, not an exception, not a decline and not a reason to resend.
basis: section:4.3 A Missing Answer Comes Back as null

aspects.says: Many threads share one link and each gets its own answer, matched by a key, whatever order the host answers in.
basis: section:4.2 Every Thread Gets Its Own Answer
aspects.reason: the matching is QMUX's own behaviour, which the reader cannot get wrong in code; the key is practised in unit c12's gateway practice

aspects.says: A MUXPool uses its first connected member under primary-secondary, and with none it keeps checking until the timeout and returns null.
basis: section:4.7.1 A Pool Takes the Name's Place

aspects.says: QMUX's in queue is the adaptor's out queue and the other way round; copied unchanged, every request times out without leaving the JVM and without an error.
basis: section:4.1 QMUX Sits on the Adaptor's Queues, Crossed

aspects.says: Each link numbers its messages from one counter that is atomic, outlives the process and wraps from 999999 to 000001.
basis: section:4.6 Each Link Numbers Its Own Messages
